newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Nov PPI advances 0.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Nov PPI advances 0.4 percent.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported that November producer prices rose by 0.4 percent after a 0.4 percent rise in the prior month. Experts had expected producer prices to advance by 0.3 percent in November.

DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "The core performance was actually pretty good. We had a 0.1 percent increase, so I suspect that after some initial fluctuations, the market will probably come to find comfort in this number."

WARD MCCARTHY, MANAGING DIRECTOR, STONE & MCCARTHY RESEARCH ASSOCIATES INC: "The report is not too bad. The overall rate was a little spunkier than expected. Car prices were at the heart of it. The core rate showed its lowest year-over-year rise since July 1994. That's indicative of generally soothing inflation numbers."

RAPHAEL MARRONE, MONEY MARKET ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL: "Its a good core number, that is what the market will be looking at. It will discount the (overall) number which was up 0.4 percent. Energy was up 2.3 percent, so that is the main contibutor.

"The report showed inflationary pressures in the pipeline are minimal. The overall outlook is that producer price inflation is well-behaved and any pressure that is out there is narrowly confined to the energy sector."
MICHELLE LAUGHLIN, CHIEF TREASURY MARKET STRATEGIST, PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES INC: "It's a neutral number -- still consistent with a fairly benign inflation outlook.
"We didn't see a reversal in auto prices as we had feared. So you end up with a number close to trend.

"Energy prices continue to be a little bit of a problem. I think we'll some moderation, but it might not happen until we get into early 1997. We continue to see a pickup in oil prices into December, so it continues to be a nagging problem."
DAVID WYSS, RESEARCH DIRECTOR AT DRI/MCGRAW HILL: "Generally, the core rate should be the headline, it's not but it should be, and that is up 0.1 (percent), which should be good news for the market.
"The core rate is up 0.6 percent on the year; I mean there is no inflation out there except for food and energy. And the big energy price increase I believe is temporary -- oil prices have soared.
"It should be good news bond market."

DAVID SLOAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A. INC: "The rise (in the November PPI) is led by energy. Elsewhere the figures were pretty soft. Given that oil prices have come off their highs, there's little to be alarmed about in these figures. The core PPI was up 0.1 percent, which is pretty good given the fact we got a 0.5 percent rise in car prices, which are volatile. Excluding cars, there's very little inflationary pressure (in the core PPI).
"On the three-month trend on core PPI, really the trend in the core rate is running at an increase of less than 0.1 percent a month.

"The PPI at the crude stage of production was up 0.8 percent but ex-food and energy, prices at the crude (early) stage of production were down 0.3 percent. As far as the intermediate stage of production, there's little inflationary risk there as well."
